findings.title: SOQL Injection
findings.explanation: The SOQL query is constructed using string concatenation, which can lead to SOQL injection if the searchKey is not properly sanitized.
findings.remediation: Use bind variables instead of string concatenation to prevent SOQL injection.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS violations
findings.explanation: The method does not enforce Field-Level Security (FLS) on the StageName field, potentially allowing users to update fields they shouldn't.
findings.remediation: Use the getSObjectType().getDescribe().fields.getMap() method to enforce FLS on the StageName field.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS violations
findings.explanation: The method does not enforce Field-Level Security (FLS) on the Phone field before updating it.
findings.remediation: Use the Schema.SObjectType.Contact.fields.Phone.isUpdateable() check to enforce FLS on the Phone field.

findings.title: FLS not enforced
findings.explanation: The code updates the 'Status' field without enforcing Field-Level Security (FLS). This can allow users to modify fields they shouldn't have access to.
findings.remediation: Use the 'SObject.get' and 'SObject.put' methods to enforce FLS.

findings.title: SOQL Injection
findings.explanation: The SOQL query is vulnerable to SOQL injection as it directly interpolates the lastName parameter without any sanitization or escaping.
findings.remediation: Use a parameterized SOQL query or escape the lastName parameter to prevent SOQL injection.
